metadata.title: Claude, Launch Your Agent.
metadata.subtitle: The Launch-Your-Agent Skill (Claude Managed Agents)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you tell Claude to launch your agent on Claude Managed Agents, does Claude improvise the build, or follow a fixed sequence — and what actually gets launched first? Lands the carry-out that launching your agent gets you a v0 in your own account, not a finished product, and anything bigger is earned through grading and iteration.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes telling Claude to launch your agent means it improvises the build. It doesn't — it follows fixed steps, in order. So: does launching my agent mean Claude follows fixed steps, not guesswork?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is called launch-your-agent. The SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set, written in plain language — no hidden logic, no code Claude has to guess at. Claude reads the file, then acts on it. The file is the program.

Inside the SKILL.md is a Steps section — the pipeline. Claude reads each step and executes it, in order. For this skill, the steps are: find out what the founder wants to build, scope a v0, launch it into their account, grade the result, and iterate. If it should run on a schedule, that becomes a scheduled deployment, with anything bigger laid out as v1 and v2. Execution is linear — no branching, unless a step says so.

Because launch-your-agent is written as a fixed specification, not open-ended judgment, it behaves the same way every time: same input, same output, every run. That also marks its edge — Claude only does what the SKILL.md actually specifies. Ask it to do something the steps don't cover, and that request falls outside the skill entirely.
Telling Claude to launch your agent doesn't launch a finished product — it launches a v0 into your account, then earns anything bigger through grading and iteration.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to help a technical founder build whatever they want on Claude Managed Agents — an internal worker, a piece of their product, or a customer-facing agent. Read the launch-your-agent skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That clause matters — asking Claude to explain first surfaces the fixed steps before it starts running them.
